structural_reading.substrate: the closed carrier-tensor ledger (162); the substrate is identified, not posited
structural_reading.graviton: the shared overlap between the two carrier-tensor sides (18 = alpha_H * D^2); the coupling at the boundary
structural_reading.matter_energy: the symmetric difference of the carrier-tensor inventory (126); what is uniquely on one side or the other, not shared
structural_reading.capacity: the union of the carrier-tensor inventory (144 = R^2); the writable address space with each element counted once
structural_reading.load_bearing_composition: capacity = matter_energy + graviton (144 = 126 + 18); the structural statement that mass + graviton = total writable space
structural_reading.sam_substrate_first_ontology: Sharpened from a postulate ('substrate is the primitive object') into a derived identification ('substrate = closed carrier-tensor ledger')

downstream_implications.higgs_derivation: H_native = |A delta B| = symmetric difference = 126; H_reveal = H_native - D^2/R surface debit = 125.25 GeV. This gives CR092a / CR120b a cleaner upstream than 'R^2(1-2^-D)' which is now derived as the symmetric difference of the substrate ledger.
downstream_implications.higgs_as_gravity_reframe: The graviton IS the shared overlap (18). It is not released by the Higgs; it IS the coupling at the boundary that the Higgs splits across. This sharpens 'Higgs gives gravity, not mass' from a slogan to a structural statement: matter-energy = unique substance (symmetric difference); graviton = shared substance (overlap); Higgs scalar = the unique-substance energy expression.
downstream_implications.manuscript_section_zero: Substrate framing can be restated: 'The substrate is the closed carrier-tensor ledger (162 = R^2 * 9/8). It is not posited; it is identified.'
